source.title: Understanding Flatness in Generative Models: Its Role and Benefits
source.authors: Taehwan Lee; Kyeongkook Seo; Jaejun Yoo; Sung Whan Yoon

record.tranche_reason: Tests flatness-promoting methods on diffusion models and reports generative performance, exposure-bias, and quantization outcomes; these settings and measures are outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for diffusion models, not the supervised natural-label generalization settings in the versions. Its own flatness and generative-performance findings are captured under fits_no_version. Cited supervised-learning results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests flatness interventions in diffusion models, but none of V1–V8. Its LPF measurements, generative FID, exposure-bias proxy and quantization results do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus classifier train–test error gaps. The theoretical distribution-robustness argument also addresses a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SAM promotes flatter diffusion-model minima more effectively than the tested averaging methods, with improved generative performance, reduced exposure bias and greater quantization robustness. They also present a theoretical link to robustness against distribution perturbations. Their testing-versus-training comparison concerns predicted-noise trajectories, not classifier error gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Diffusion-model score/noise prediction and generative FID, exposure-bias, and quantization measures; the listed originals and versions concern supervised natural-label generalization or classifier train-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and sampling timestep affect FID; the paper reports differing results across CIFAR-10, LSUN Tower, and FFHQ and between 20- and 100-step sampling. SAM strength ρ was tuned over [1e−1, 1e−2, 1e−3].

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 with 20 sampling steps, ADM+SAM has FID 9.01 versus ADM's 34.47. Its LPF is 0.063 versus 0.097 without averaging.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this diffusion setup, SAM improves generative FID and produces a flatter measured loss landscape.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM sampling trajectories have predicted-noise norms closer to the training trajectory; Table 1 reports gaps of +3.32 for ADM+SAM and +11.39 for ADM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM reduces the reported exposure-bias proxy in the tested diffusion setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct 8-bit quantization changes CIFAR-10 20-step FID from 34.47 to 48.02 for ADM and from 9.01 to 8.94 for ADM+SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM-trained diffusion models better preserve generative performance under direct parameter quantization in this setting.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2025
record.problems: The tested models are unconditional diffusion models and the outcomes are generative measures, so the results do not directly establish the supervised natural-label generalization claims. Reported results do not provide uncertainty estimates. Some outcomes, including the exposure-bias comparison, are presented in figures without numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 contains additional algorithm-by-dataset-by-timestep FID results, and Table 4 gives additional quantization comparisons. These were not extracted to keep the record focused on representative baseline/SAM comparisons; no supervised version-specific result was omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning; all experiments use Adam.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus classifier train–test error gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification. None of the supplied versions receives a verdict. All row states are cannot_determine relative to those versions; this does not dispute the reported diffusion-model improvements. No additional version-bearing results were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers on image labels.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization on classification or language benchmarks.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps in supervised classifiers.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy changes.

rows.subject: +SAM
rows.operation_detail: L2 norm of predicted noise during sampling compared with training curve
rows.measure: Predicted-noise L2 norm over timesteps and its gap from the training curve
rows.note: Text says SAM models maintained norms closer to training; this is exposure bias, not the supervised train-test error gap.
rows.check: This measures sampling-versus-training predicted-noise norms, not a classifier generalization gap. Numeric summaries are available in Table 1: the reported norm gap is +11.39 for ADM and +3.32 for ADM+SAM, so 'figure only' is incomplete. Section 4.1 describes squared norms, whereas Figure 6 and Table 1 label norms; preserve that reporting ambiguity.
